solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fat Alexander refused to do so after siege

definitions.meaning: a roll of fat round the waist

definitions.text: Alexander refused to do so after siege
definitions.meaning: Alexander the Great besieged the city of Tyre and, once it fell, showed it no mercy

explanation.surface: Someone called Alexander wouldn't lose weight after a long struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as SPARE TYRE: Alexander the Great took the Phoenician city of Tyre after a seven-month siege in 332 BC and did not spare it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is the everyday British idiom for a roll of flab round the middle.

clue.text: Lets go of instrument in recital

indicators.note: in recital means as it is spoken out, so the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: a sax is a saxophone, a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A player drops an instrument during a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recital' looks like a concert, but it signals saying the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from a job, which is letting them go.

clue.text: Answer, pithy, about crop at the heart of rural economy

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the inner letters

parts.note: gnomic means terse and aphoristic, pithy

indicators.note: at the heart means only the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A short reply about the main crop in the farm economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop at the heart' reads as the crop central to farming; it is the middle of the word crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production, so the adjective concerns farming.

clue.text: Banned setter turning round, getting shoved outside

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: the shoving word goes outside, wrapped round the ring

parts.note: to barge is to shove
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is barred after spinning round and being pushed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade, so embargoed means prohibited.

clue.text: I don't know what to say to driver after trip?

definitions.text: I don't know what to say
definitions.meaning: ... admits you are stumped by a question
a passenger, after a journey, might thank the driver for having brought them to their destination

explanation.surface: A passenger is lost for words to thank the driver after a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of admitting defeat, as when a question leaves one stumped.

clue.text: Pick Caesar, say, to pen grand quote about kind of force

parts.note: to elect is to pick

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Caesar is an example of a Roman
G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Choose Caesar to write a quotation on some kind of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing; it means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Electromagnetism is one of the four fundamental forces of physics, alongside gravity and the nuclear forces.

clue.text: Heroine doomed to die, and not an old lady

parts.note: nor means and not
one's old lady is one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: A tragic heroine is marked out for death, and she is not elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma, in Bellini's opera, goes to the pyre at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's druid priestess Norma ends her opera mounting a funeral pyre, a heroine fated to perish.

clue.text: Asian statesman's game bird rising first

indicators.note: first means the bird comes before the game
rising in a down entry means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a hen is a bird
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A politician's game bird flies up to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister of independent India.

clue.text: Bones almost set, say, by head of institute

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set

indicators.note: head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Broken bones are nearly set, perhaps by the director of an institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests setting a fracture; it is a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; the plural is radii.

clue.text: After a jumble sale: gain what a number will bring

indicators.note: after means the shuffled letters follow the single letter
a jumble mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a rummage sale, you gain what a few items will fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but a numb-er, something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is loss of pain sensation, which a numbing drug brings about.

clue.text: Tundra dweller in scarf and tie, about to strip off

indicators.note: stripping off a word's coverings leaves its inner letters, so each of the three words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone in the far north wrapped in scarf and tie is about to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to strip off' applies to all three words: sCARf, tIe and aBOUt.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, an animal of the Arctic treeless plains.

clue.text: English buddy welcoming days one may eat grub

indicators.note: welcoming means the outer word takes the other in, holding it inside

parts.note: china (from rhyming slang china plate, mate) means buddy

explanation.surface: An English friend has people over for some days, one of whom might eat anything.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, feeds on ants, termites and insect larvae, which are grubs.

clue.text: I will be rejected by older gent abroad

indicators.note: being rejected by a word means being thrown out of it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: senior means older
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to be turned down by an older man overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title for a gentleman, so a man in a foreign land.

clue.text: Firing some workmen thus in garage

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dismissing some of the mechanics working this way in a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' reads as sacking; here it means firing up, exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to fill them with eagerness, so firing is a synonym for enthusing.

clue.text: Musical group straighten out Beethoven's Sixth

parts.note: to comb hair is to straighten it out

indicators.note: sixth here means the sixth letter of the word, not the Pastoral symphony

explanation.surface: An ensemble tidies up its performance of Beethoven's Sixth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Sixth' suggests the Pastoral Symphony; it is just the sixth letter of Beethoven.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small jazz or dance band, a kind of musical ensemble.

clue.text: Red stone concludes religious ritual, on leaving

indicators.note: concludes means the stone comes at the end
leaving means the word given goes out of it

parts.note: communion is the Christian sacrament of the Eucharist
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A red-coloured gem ends a church service, on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a long-standing label for a communist, from the colour of the revolutionary flag.

clue.text: Forged euros sold, evading detection?

indicators.note: forged things are made up or faked, so these letters are hammered into a new order

explanation.surface: Counterfeit currency sold without being spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: something with no smell evades detection by the nose, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no scent, an odourless thing cannot be picked up by sniffing, so it goes unnoticed.

clue.text: Criminal's item in court, veneer oddly scratched

parts.note: a racket is used on a tennis or squash court

indicators.note: with the odd letters scratched out, only the even ones are left

explanation.surface: A villain's piece of evidence in a courtroom has a strangely scratched surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest racket, such as extortion, so is a crook.

clue.text: Latino's fare from China, deal that's beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Mexican food from a Chinese deal that cannot be bettered.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican rolled tortilla with filling, food from Latin America.

clue.text: First guy with case of insomnia after computer nut

indicators.note: after puts the computer word in front of the rest, which follows it

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
Adam was the first man

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An insomniac uses a computer after an early man, a story of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is a round Australian nut with a hard shell.

clue.text: Officer repeatedly needing a drink

indicators.note: repeatedly says the officer is given more than once, so the same piece comes again

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer keeps requiring a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' means CO, a commanding officer, is written twice before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder.

clue.text: New Order plugs new tune that's not recorded

indicators.note: plugs means the order goes into the other letters like a stopper in a hole
new here means the letters are made anew in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
a writ is a court order

explanation.surface: The band New Order feature on a fresh tune that has never been put down on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: New Order is a Manchester band, but the words split: 'New' is N, 'Order' a court writ. The second 'new' is the anagram signal for N plus the tune letters, giving UNTEN, which 'plugs' fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwritten is not set down on paper, so it exists without any record.

clue.text: Offbeat fashion label in fashion

indicators.note: in means the label goes inside the other word

parts.note: a way of doing something is a fashion or manner
CK is Calvin Klein, the fashion brand

explanation.surface: An eccentric designer label is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'fashion' is a manner, not style.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacky and offbeat are both informal words for eccentric or quirky.

clue.text: One's thick papers and current books

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: one who is thick, a dimwit

parts.note: ID means identity papers
I is the symbol for electric current
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: One person is made dense by newspapers, current affairs and books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's thick' reads as a statement but works as a noun: one that is thick.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, someone who is dim-witted.

clue.text: Poet's material taken from the Orient

indicators.note: taken from the east means read from the right-hand end in this across entry, so backwards

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A writer's fabric is imported from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Orient' is the east, the right side of a map, so the fabric is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the modernist author of The Waste Land and Four Quartets.

clue.text: Tasty plant is a passing phenomenon, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: time is a thing that passes

explanation.surface: A trendy herb is just a passing fad, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used to flavour food.

clue.text: Lean cold cuts forming a row

indicators.note: cuts means the letter slices into the middle of the other word

parts.note: things in line are forming a row

explanation.surface: Slices of lean cold meat are laid out in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean cold cuts' reads as low-fat sliced meat; 'Lean' is a verb, and 'cuts' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean and to incline both mean to slope or tilt to one side.

clue.text: Those people about to knock Freudian process

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: they means those people
to rap is to knock

explanation.surface: People are set to criticise the methods of psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis, Freud's talking cure, is a form of psychological treatment.

clue.text: Meeting with Tory's too utterly devoid of love

indicators.note: utterly devoid of means every single one goes, so all of the given letter is stripped out

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O; every O goes

explanation.surface: A Conservative's rendezvous is entirely loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' means all three Os in TORYSTOO go, leaving the remaining letters in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret rendezvous, usually between lovers.

clue.text: Disparage old flame? My one scoffed

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
cor is an exclamation like my!
I is the Roman numeral one
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: A former partner says nasty things as someone wolfs down food.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate is to criticise savagely, literally to strip the skin off someone.
